title: Scheduler probe-windowing causes burst-scale stalls and p99 spikes — retro & remediation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During a capacity burst on hosted inference, a recent change to the scheduler's probe windowing heuristic caused repeated stalls in kernel promotion and batch servicing. This produced transient p95/p99 latency spikes (~2--8x baseline) for several high-volume customer routes during scale events and degraded serving throughput for ~18 minutes in a subset of regions.
timeline: 2026-03-09 05:12 UTC — Canary rollout of scheduler probe-windowing change (patch: runtime#7421) begins.

2026-03-09 05:49 UTC — Autoscaler triggered additional workers; observed repeated kernel promotion delays and batch eviction spikes.
2026-03-09 06:05 UTC — Rollout paused; emergency rollback initiated for probe-windowing change to previous parameters.
2026-03-09 06:16 UTC — Rollback completed; metrics begin to normalize, p99 returned to baseline by 06:30 UTC.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC — Incident triage initiated, investigation assigned to runtime and scheduler owners.
investigation_summary: Root cause: the new probe-windowing parameter reduced the probe sampling frequency and introduced a probe hysteresis window that overlapped with the autoscaler "capacity fence" logic. During burst events probes were deferred, leaving the scheduler unaware of recently warmed kernels and causing it to continue dispatching to cold paths. This led to frequent batch evictions and repeated kernel reinitialization (KV cache churn). Secondary contributors: insufficient canary coverage for high burst patterns and missing synthetic tests for probe-window/scale interactions.
mitigation_steps: Immediate rollback of probe-windowing parameter change (completed 2026-03-09).
Short-term: tighten canary gating to include simulated burst traffic in NY and EU canaries (ETA: 2026-03-17).
Medium-term: add scheduler metric 'probe_deferred_count' and 'probe_vs_scale_mismatch' and alert when probe deferrals coincide with scale events (ETA: 2026-03-24).
Medium-term: introduce a probe-promote fastpath during active autoscale windows that forces a synchronous probe in the first 200ms of worker attachment (design doc in progress).
